## NODE char_odysseus Character "Odysseus" "Odyssey" "book 9"
summary: King of Ithaca, son of Laertes and Anticleia, hero of the Trojan War and protagonist of the Odyssey.

## NODE char_penelope Character "Penelope" "Odyssey" "book 1"
summary: Wife of Odysseus and queen of Ithaca, known for her fidelity and cleverness.

## NODE char_telemachus Character "Telemachus" "Odyssey" "book 1"
summary: Son of Odysseus and Penelope, who searches for his father in the early books.

## NODE char_laertes Character "Laertes" "Odyssey" "book 24"
summary: Father of Odysseus and former king of Ithaca.

## NODE place_ithaca Place "Ithaca" "Odyssey" "book 1"
summary: The island kingdom of Odysseus on the Ionian coast.

## NODE place_troy Place "Troy" "Iliad" "book 1"
summary: The walled city besieged by the Greeks for ten years.

## NODE event_trojan_war Event "The Trojan War" "Iliad" "book 1"
summary: A ten-year war between Greeks and Trojans, triggered by the abduction of Helen.

## NODE obj_bow Object "Bow of Odysseus" "Odyssey" "book 21"
summary: The great bow of Odysseus, used in the contest of the axes.

## NODE concept_xenia Concept "Xenia" "Odyssey" "book 9"
summary: The Greek code of guest-friendship, a sacred bond between host and guest.

## NODE char_polyphemus Character "Polyphemus" "Odyssey" "book 9"
summary: A Cyclops, son of Poseidon, blinded by Odysseus.

## EDGE edge_odysseus_spouse char_odysseus SPOUSE_OF char_penelope "Odyssey" "book 1"

## EDGE edge_odysseus_xenia char_odysseus ASSOCIATED_WITH concept_xenia "Odyssey" "book 9"

## NODE char_athena Character "Athena" "Odyssey" "book 13"
summary: Goddess of wisdom and warfare; daughter of Zeus; champion and guide of Odysseus throughout his journey home; disguises herself as Mentor.

## NODE char_poseidon Character "Poseidon" "Odyssey" "book 9"
summary: God of the sea and earthquakes; father of the Cyclops Polyphemus; delays Odysseus's return for a decade in vengeance for blinding his son.

## NODE char_zeus Character "Zeus" "Odyssey" "book 1"
summary: King of the gods, ruler of the sky; decrees Odysseus's fate; sends Hermes to Calypso to release Odysseus.

## NODE char_circe Character "Circe" "Odyssey" "book 10"
summary: Sorceress on the island of Aeaea; turned Odysseus's men into swine; became Odysseus's lover and guide for a year; daughter of the sun god Helios.

## NODE char_calypso Character "Calypso" "Odyssey" "book 5"
summary: Sea nymph on the island of Ogygia; held Odysseus captive for seven years; offered him immortality to stay; released him by Zeus's command.

## NODE char_hermes Character "Hermes" "Odyssey" "book 5"
summary: Messenger god; sent by Zeus to tell Calypso to release Odysseus; gave Odysseus the herb moly to resist Circe's magic.

## NODE place_aeaea Place "Aeaea" "Odyssey" "book 10"
summary: The island home of the sorceress Circe; where Odysseus's men were turned into swine and where he stayed for a year.

## NODE place_ogygia Place "Ogygia" "Odyssey" "book 5"
summary: The island home of the nymph Calypso; where Odysseus was held for seven years; a remote, hidden island far from all.

## NODE place_underworld Place "The Underworld (Hades)" "Odyssey" "book 11"
summary: The realm of the dead; Odysseus journeys here to consult the prophet Tiresias; meets his mother, Achilles, and Agamemnon among the dead.

## NODE char_tiresias Character "Tiresias" "Odyssey" "book 11"
summary: The blind prophet of Thebes; Odysseus consults him in the underworld; foretells the rest of his journey and warns of the cattle of the sun god.

## NODE event_blinding Event "Blinding of Polyphemus" "Odyssey" "book 9"
summary: Odysseus and his men drive a heated stake into the eye of the Cyclops Polyphemus, allowing them to escape his cave; this act provokes Poseidon's wrath.

## NODE event_return Event "The nostos of Odysseus" "Odyssey" "book 23"
summary: Odysseus's twenty-year return from Troy to Ithaca; he disguises himself as a beggar, wins the bow contest, slaughters the suitors, and is reunited with Penelope.

## NODE concept_nostos Concept "Nostos" "Odyssey" "book 1"
summary: The Greek concept of homecoming; the central theme of the Odyssey; a perilous sea journey fraught with divine obstacles and the temptation of forgetting one's homeland.
